newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German December industrial output.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German December industrial output.

text.p: Following are reactions to German December industrial production data, which showed a 1.4-percent gain month-on-month and a 3.3-percent rise year-on-year. November's output increases were revised down to 0.9 percent month-on-month and 0.7 percent year-on-year.

UWE ANGENENDT, BHF-BANK: "They are surprisingly strong figures, but they should be treated with caution because they contain many estimates. I don't think they will lead to a correction of the 1.4-percent German GDP rise reported for 1996. The November data have been revised down strongly. So overall, there is an unchanged picture of economic stagnation or a minor contraction in the fourth quarter. The west German data were not as positive as the east German figures."

MATHIAS HAFFNER, BARCLAYS DE ZOETE WEDD: "The figure is clearly better than expected. But the rise was driven by construction activitiy and mining rather than by manufacturing, and it would be better if it were the other way around. We still see final quarter GDP growth at 0.2 percent. We had been thinking about revising it down to zero, but we won't do that now. The (December) production data will certainly be revised. I don't know in what direction, but it must be taken at face value, and it's positive."
The following comments were made to Reuters Financial Television:

HANS-JUERGEN MELTZER, DEUTSCHE BANK RESEARCH: "It is a positive surprise. The figure suggests that the level of industrial production was the same in the fourth quarter as in the third quarter, and that is good news. But the crucial number will be the labour market data."
TIMO KLEIN, MMS INTERNATIONAL: "I am surprised, and the most surprising thing is the jump in construction output. The bounce back expected for January happened already in December."

MICHAEL CLAUSS, CREDIT SUISSE FIRST BOSTON: "The figure is higher than expected, but no trend reversal. Bund market has taken idea on board that figures (are) less important than order data. There are signs of further weakness expected going into the first quarter."
